title: 2020年12月 第2套

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This is unbelievable.
lines.translation: W：这真是难以置信。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Unlike any video game I've ever played before, it's so boring, yet so relaxing at the same time.
lines.translation: 它和我以前玩过的任何电子游戏都不一样，既无聊，却又让人感到放松。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: How did you hear about this driving simulator?
lines.translation: 你是怎么听说这个驾驶模拟器的？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: My brother introduced it to me last year.
lines.translation: M：我哥哥去年介绍给我的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I was surprised to find how educational and realistic it was.
lines.translation: 我很惊讶地发现它既有教育意义，又非常逼真。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's called Euro Truck Simulator, but they have other versions as well for America and so on.
lines.translation: 它叫《欧洲卡车模拟》，不过他们也有美国版之类的其他版本。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I was really drawn to the scenery.
lines.translation: 我真的很喜欢里面的风景。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The routes go through parts of the country you don't normally see as a tourist.
lines.translation: 路线会经过一些游客通常不会去的地方。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Yeah, I can see that.
lines.translation: W：是啊，我能看出来。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It seems so simple, just transporting cargo from point A to point B, driving from one city to another.
lines.translation: 它看起来很简单，就是把货物从A点运到B点，从一个城市开到另一个城市。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But I really appreciate all the details that go into the game.
lines.translation: 但我真的很欣赏这款游戏中的各种细节。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's even given me a new appreciation for the logistics industry and traffic on the road.
lines.translation: 它甚至让我开始更加了解物流行业以及道路上的交通状况。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I completely agree.
lines.translation: M：我完全同意。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: My brother also introduced me to some videos of someone that streams their game online.
lines.translation: 我哥哥还给我介绍了一些视频，视频里有人在网上直播玩这个游戏。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It was fascinating to watch, really.
lines.translation: 看起来真的很有意思。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This guy drove very carefully, obeyed all the road signs and traffic rules—such a contrast to most violent games.
lines.translation: 那个人开车非常小心，遵守所有道路标志和交通规则，这和大多数暴力游戏形成了鲜明对比。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Honestly, playing has inspired me to look into the industry more.
lines.translation: W：说实话，玩这个游戏让我产生了进一步了解这个行业的想法。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I've read articles about how self-driving trucks may soon be available and could greatly impact cargo logistics.
lines.translation: 我读过一些文章，说自动驾驶卡车可能很快就会投入使用，并可能对货物运输产生重大影响。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Considering all that goes into driving these larger vehicles, it's amazing that we could soon have that kind of technology.
lines.translation: 考虑到驾驶这些大型车辆需要处理的各种情况，我们很快就能拥有那样的技术，真是令人惊叹。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Ha.

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I've got one step further.
lines.translation: 我还差一步

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I registered to take a safe driving course to improve my real-life driving skills.
lines.translation: 我注册了安全驾驶课程 以提高我的真实驾驶技能

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In a way, I feel like I have a head start compared to other students in the class.
lines.translation: 从某种意义上说,我觉得我比班里其他学生 有了个先入之见。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Playing this video game has given me some maneuvering practices already.
lines.translation: 玩这个游戏 已经给我一些动作练习了

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I'm not sure how accurate the video game is compared to real-life situations.
lines.translation: W：我不确定这款电子游戏与现实情况相比有多准确。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But if it results in more drivers looking both ways before entering an intersection, I'd say that's a positive outcome.
lines.translation: 但如果它能让更多司机在驶入十字路口前先左右观察，我会说这是一种积极的结果。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
lines.translation: 问题1至4是基于你刚才听到的谈话

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 1. What are the speakers mainly talking about?
lines.translation: 第 1 题：说话者主要在谈论什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 2. What does the man say about the driving simulator?
lines.translation: 第 2 题：男士对驾驶模拟器有何评价?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Question three.
lines.translation: 问题三。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 3. What does the woman say she really appreciates?
lines.translation: 第 3 题：女士说她真正欣赏的是什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 4. What outcome does the woman expect from the driving simulator?
lines.translation: 第 4 题：女士期望从驾驶模拟器中获得什么结果?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Conversation two.
lines.translation: 对话二

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: How do you like being self-employed?
lines.translation: 你喜欢做个体经营者吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: There are obvious benefits, though I don't seem to have the freedom I anticipated as I just don't seem able to decline work offers.
lines.translation: 这当然有明显的好处，不过我好像没有获得原本预想的自由，因为我似乎根本没法拒绝工作机会。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And working alone, there have been times when I've found that money alone provides insufficient motivation.
lines.translation: 而且一个人工作时，我有时会发现，光靠钱并不足以提供动力。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Have you experienced the same since you began working for yourself?
lines.translation: 自从你开始为自己工作以来，你也有过同样的经历吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Sometimes, yes.
lines.translation: 有时候，是的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Unlike the rest of the workforce who have managers to prompt motivation whenever they're feeling lazy or bored, we self-employed workers perform our jobs without a manager to lift our spirits.
lines.translation: 其他劳动者懒散或感到无聊时，会有经理来督促他们、激发他们的动力；而我们这些个体经营者没有经理来鼓舞士气，只能独自完成工作。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: There's no one around to offer praise or initiate collaboration, no one to make greater use of our interests and talents.
lines.translation: 身边没有人给予表扬或发起合作，也没有人更充分地利用我们的兴趣和才能。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That's a fact.
lines.translation: 确实如此。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Not every manager behaves with such awareness and care, of course.
lines.translation: 当然，并不是每个经理都能如此体察下属、如此体贴。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And certainly not all managers have a clue how to motivate people.
lines.translation: 而且，肯定也不是所有经理都知道该如何激励员工。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Still, having a manager nearby at least indicates there's an opportunity they'll be decent enough to look out for you when your energy and focus begin to deplete.
lines.translation: 不过，身边有个经理，至少说明当你的精力和注意力开始消耗殆尽时，对方有可能足够体面，愿意照顾你。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The motivator I value most is autonomy.
lines.translation: 我最看重的激励因素是自主性。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I've learned not to sacrifice my prized autonomy by working all hours of the day and by saying yes to every client request.
lines.translation: 我已经学会了不为了整天工作、也不为了答应客户的每一个要求，而牺牲自己珍视的自主权。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Yes.
lines.translation: 是的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I need to remind myself that I selected this lifestyle for the independence.
lines.translation: 我需要提醒自己，我选择这种生活方式就是为了独立。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I don't miss aspects of permanent full-time employment I disliked, such as the office politics, job insecurity, inflexible hours and so on.
lines.translation: 我并不怀念那些我不喜欢的全职长期雇佣工作的方面，比如办公室政治、工作不稳定、工作时间不灵活等等。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I wouldn't mind a bit more in the form of praise though, praise which is on the record.
lines.translation: 不过，如果能多得到一些表扬，我倒不会介意，尤其是正式记录在案的表扬。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That'll come with time.
lines.translation: 这会随着时间而来。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Relatedness is inevitably cultivated via human interaction.
lines.translation: 人与人之间的互动必然会培养关系联结感。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Engaging with clients, getting written testimony and recommendations, staying in contact with clients afterwards, these are things you'll find will come in due course and provide you with motivation.
lines.translation: 与客户交流、获得书面证明和推荐、之后继续与客户保持联系，这些事情你会发现都会逐渐出现，并为你提供动力。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You're right.
lines.translation: 你说得对。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That's an area I do need to put some more effort into—building closer relationships with those who engage my services and skills.
lines.translation: 这方面我确实需要多下些功夫，也就是和那些聘用我的服务和技能的人建立更亲密的关系。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 5. What does the man say about his life of being self-employed?
lines.translation: 第 5 题：男士如何评价他自雇的生活?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 6. What does the man say about managers?
lines.translation: 第 6 题：男士对管理者有何看法?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 7. What do both speakers value most about self-employment?
lines.translation: 第 7 题：两位说话者最看重自雇的哪一点?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 8. On what point does the man agree with the woman?
lines.translation: 第 8 题：男士在哪一点上赞同女士的观点?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Section B. Directions.
lines.translation: B节. 指示。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: this section you'll hear two passages.
lines.translation: 这部分你会听到两段

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: At the end of each passage you'll hear three or four questions.
lines.translation: 每条路的尽头 你会听到三四个问题

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
lines.translation: 发言的通过和提问将只讲一次。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: After you hear a question,
lines.translation: 在你听到一个问题之后

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
lines.translation: 您必须选择四个选择中的最佳答案,即A、B、C和D。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the centre.
lines.translation: 在答题表一中标出相应的字母,在中间线上标出单行。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Weather is a constant force in our lives, but there's little marketing research on how it affects businesses.
lines.translation: 天气是我们生活中的一股恒定力量 但对于它如何影响企业 几乎没有什么营销研究

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Now, a new study reveals how sunny and snowy conditions influence consumer behavior.
lines.translation: 如今，一项新研究揭示了晴朗和下雪的天气状况如何影响消费者行为。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Those weather conditions trigger consumers to mentally visualize using products associated with the respective weather.
lines.translation: 这些天气状况会促使消费者在脑海中想象使用与相应天气相关的产品。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This leads to consumers placing a higher value on those products.
lines.translation: 这会使消费者更加看重这些产品。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That is, they're willing to pay more money for them.
lines.translation: 也就是说，他们愿意为这些产品支付更多的钱。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But the correlation is only found with products related to being outside.
lines.translation: 但这种相关性仅存在于与户外活动有关的产品中。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: How does this work?
lines.translation: 这是如何起作用的呢？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Researchers give the example of a beach towel.
lines.translation: 研究人员以沙滩巾为例。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: On a sunny day, consumers who see that product are not just looking at the towel itself, they are likely imagining themselves lying on the towel in the sun.
lines.translation: 在晴天，看到这件产品的消费者不只是看着沙滩巾本身，他们很可能会想象自己躺在阳光下的沙滩巾上。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This mental picture of using the towel increases the value of the product in the consumers' mind.
lines.translation: 这样一幅使用沙滩巾的心理画面，会提高消费者心目中这件产品的价值。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Researchers put forward the following hypothesis to explain their findings.
lines.translation: 研究人员提出了以下假设来解释他们的发现。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They think the mental picture works in sunshine and snow because these weather conditions have a positive association with outside activities.
lines.translation: 他们认为，阳光和雪天之所以会产生这种心理画面，是因为这些天气状况与户外活动之间存在积极联系。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The effect is not seen with rainy weather.
lines.translation: 下雨天气则不会产生这种影响。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Researchers assert this is because there aren't many activities that are enabled by rain.
lines.translation: 研究人员认为，这是因为雨天能开展的活动并不多。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Most products associated with rain, like umbrellas, are only used for protection from the weather, and not for any activities.
lines.translation: 大多数与下雨有关的产品，如雨伞，都只是用来抵御天气影响，而不是用于进行任何活动。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Researchers believe that companies that sell a wide array of products online can benefit most from the insights this study provides.
lines.translation: 研究人员认为，在线销售种类繁多产品的公司最能从这项研究提供的洞见中受益。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Online sellers often use complex mathematical formulas to determine what products to feature and how to price these products.
lines.translation: 在线卖家通常会使用复杂的数学公式来确定重点展示哪些产品以及如何为这些产品定价。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Incorporating more data about weather would allow them to make better decisions.
lines.translation: 纳入更多有关天气的数据，将使他们能够作出更好的决策。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This could bolster sales.
lines.translation: 这可能会促进销售。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
lines.translation: 问题9至11是基于你刚才听到的段落。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 9. What do we learn about the findings of the new study?
lines.translation: 第 9 题：关于这项新研究的发现,我们了解到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 10. What does the passage say may increase the value of products for consumers?
lines.translation: 第 10 题：文章指出什么可能会增加产品对消费者的价值?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 11. How can the findings of the new study benefit online sellers according to the researchers?
lines.translation: 第 11 题：根据研究人员的说法,这项新研究的发现如何使在线销售商受益?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Passage 2.
lines.translation: 通行证2。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Setting the office air conditioning at about 22 degrees Celsius has become standard practice across the world.
lines.translation: 将办公室空调设定在约22摄氏度,已成为全世界的标准做法。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Numerous guidebooks across the world on heating, ventilation and air-conditioning claim office performance peaks at 22 degrees.
lines.translation: 世界各地众多有关供暖、通风和空调的指南都声称，办公室工作效率在22摄氏度时达到最高。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Many people indeed find relief from soaring summer temperatures in air-conditioned offices.
lines.translation: 事实上，许多人确实能在装有空调的办公室里缓解夏季高温带来的不适。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But recent studies have challenged the accepted wisdom that a cool office is more productive.
lines.translation: 然而，近期研究对“凉爽的办公室能提高工作效率”这一公认观点提出了质疑。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The reality is more complex.
lines.translation: 实际情况更加复杂。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Researchers conducted a review of all studies relating to air-conditioning and productivity.
lines.translation: 研究人员对所有涉及空调与工作效率的研究进行了综述。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They found that 22 degrees was probably a little chilly, even at the height of summer.
lines.translation: 他们发现，即使在盛夏，22摄氏度可能也有些凉。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: For a person dressed in typical summer clothing, an optimal range would be between 23 and 26 degrees.
lines.translation: 对于穿着典型夏装的人来说，最佳温度范围应在23至26摄氏度之间。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And people can even tolerate temperatures beyond this comfort zone as long as they can adjust their clothing and expectations.
lines.translation: 只要人们能够调整衣着和心理预期，他们甚至可以忍受超过这一舒适区的温度。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In fact, even on very hot days, it makes sense to turn the air-conditioning up.
lines.translation: 事实上，即使在非常炎热的日子里，把空调温度调高也是合理的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: People often chase just one optimum temperature, and this is understandable when people feel hot.
lines.translation: 人们往往只追求一个最佳温度，当人感到炎热时，这种做法是可以理解的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But there is a range of at least three to four degrees which does not have any adverse impact.
lines.translation: 但实际上，存在一个至少三到四摄氏度的温度范围，在这个范围内，工作效率不会受到任何不利影响。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Another issue related to this is that people can become psychologically dependent on air conditioning.
lines.translation: 与此相关的另一个问题是,人们在心理上可以依赖空调。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: If they're used to the environment which is air-conditioned, they tend to prefer lower temperatures.
lines.translation: 如果它们习惯于有空调的环境, 它们倾向于更低的温度。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But the studies found that almost all humans became accustomed to the new temperature.
lines.translation: 但研究发现几乎所有人类 都习惯了新温度

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It was only at the extreme ends of the temperature range where people's productivity suffered.
lines.translation: 只是在温度范围最极端的尽头 人们的生产力受到打击

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This range was above 26 degrees and below 19 degrees.
lines.translation: 该范围高于26度,低于19度。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 12. What is the accepted wisdom concerning the office environment?
lines.translation: 第 12 题：关于办公环境，人们普遍接受的观点是什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 13. What did researchers find from their review of all studies relating to air-conditioning and productivity?
lines.translation: 第 13 题：研究人员从他们对所有与空调和生产力相关的研究的回顾中发现了什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 14. What do we learn about using a little less air-conditioning during hot weather?
lines.translation: 第 14 题：关于在炎热天气少用一点空调,我们了解到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 15. What happens when people are used to an air-conditioned environment?
lines.translation: 第 15 题：当人们习惯了空调环境时会发生什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Section C. Directions.
lines.translation: C节. 指示。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In this section you'll hear three recordings of lectures or talks followed by three or four questions.
lines.translation: 在本节中,你们将听到三段演讲或谈话录音,然后三四个问题。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The recordings will be played only once.
lines.translation: 录音只播放一次。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: you hear a question,
lines.translation: 你听到一个问题,

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
lines.translation: 您必须选择四个选择中最好的答案, 四个选择标注为 A、 B、 C、 D 。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
lines.translation: 在答题单单行的答题表一中标出相应的字母。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Recording one.
lines.translation: 记录一。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Psychology research has tended to portray solitude as a negative experience.
lines.translation: 心理学研究往往将独处描绘成一种负面体验。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Studies conducted in the 1970s and 1990s suggested that people felt less happy when alone as compared to being with others.
lines.translation: 20世纪70年代和90年代开展的研究表明，与和他人在一起相比，人们独处时感到不那么快乐。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: However, a new paper shows an alternative view of solitude, one in which solitude can be positive.
lines.translation: 然而，一篇新的论文展现了关于独处的另一种观点，认为独处也可以是积极的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Let's start by looking at the earlier research.
lines.translation: 让我们先看看早期的研究

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It had a couple of shortcomings.
lines.translation: 它有一些缺点。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: First, it measured emotion on a scale from positive to negative, overlooking the possibility that our positive and negative emotions can fluctuate independently.
lines.translation: 首先,它从正面到负面衡量情绪,忽略了我们正面和负面情绪独立波动的可能性。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Also, it categorized emotions as simply positive or negative.
lines.translation: 而且,它把情绪归类为仅仅是正面或负面的情绪。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It didn't consider that emotions arouse us to different degrees, and that both positive and negative emotions can arouse us a lot or a little.
lines.translation: 它没有考虑到情绪会不同程度地刺激我们, 积极和消极的情绪会经常或稍稍地刺激我们。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That is, whether positive or negative, emotions can be either high-arousal or low-arousal.
lines.translation: 不管是正面的还是负面的 情绪都可能是高刺激或是低刺激

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: High-arousal emotions include excitement on the positive side or anger on the negative side, while low-arousal ones include feeling calm on the positive side or lonely on the negative.
lines.translation: 高振奋情绪包括正面的兴奋情绪或消极的愤怒情绪,而低振奋情绪的情绪包括正面的平静情绪或消极的孤独情绪。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This new research attempted to overcome these shortcomings.
lines.translation: 这项新研究试图克服这些缺陷。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Researchers began with a simple study.
lines.translation: 研究人员首先进行了一项简单的研究。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They asked participants to spend 15 minutes sitting alone without engaging in any activity, and measured how this solitude influences their emotional state.
lines.translation: 他们要求参与者独自坐着15分钟，不从事任何活动，并测量独处如何影响他们的情绪状态。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This experiment specifically aimed to determine the effect of solitude on high-arousal emotions.
lines.translation: 这项实验旨在确定独处对高唤起情绪的影响。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It looked at positive emotions such as being excited or interested, and negative emotions including being scared or distressed.
lines.translation: 研究考察了兴奋或感兴趣等积极情绪，也考察了害怕或痛苦等消极情绪。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The results were clear.
lines.translation: 结果很明确。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: After 15 minutes of solitude, the participants showed reductions in both types of emotion.
lines.translation: 独处15分钟后，参与者的这两类情绪都有所减弱。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: A second study measured the effects of solitude on low-arousal emotions.
lines.translation: 第二项研究测量了独处对低唤起情绪的影响。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: These included both positive and negative emotions, such as feeling calm, relaxed, sad or lonely.
lines.translation: 这些情绪既包括积极情绪，也包括消极情绪，例如平静、放松、悲伤或孤独感。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That experiment found that all of these emotions were increased by time alone.
lines.translation: 实验发现，独处时间的增加使所有这些情绪都增强了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Thus it seems past depictions of solitude were wrong.
lines.translation: 因此，过去对独处的描述似乎是错误的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It doesn't have a simple emotional effect that can be characterized as good or bad.
lines.translation: 独处并不会产生一种可以简单归为好或坏的情绪影响。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Rather, it changes the intensity of our inner experience.
lines.translation: 相反，它会改变我们内在体验的强度。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It amplifies quieter emotions, but it diminishes the intensity of stronger feelings.
lines.translation: 它会放大较为微弱的情绪，却会减弱较强烈感受的强度。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's worth clarifying that these findings relate to relatively brief periods of solitude.
lines.translation: 需要明确的是，这些发现与相对较短时间的独处有关。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This is distinct from prolonged loneliness.
lines.translation: 这不同于长期的孤独。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Research has demonstrated that the latter is correlated with an assortment of negative physical and psychological effects.
lines.translation: 研究表明，后者与一系列负面的生理和心理影响相关。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: How can people benefit from being alone?
lines.translation: 人们如何从独处中受益？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The findings here suggest that people can use solitude to regulate their emotions.
lines.translation: 这里的研究结果表明，人们可以利用独处来调节情绪。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Solitude can help us become quiet after excitement, calm after an angry episode, or simply feel at peace.
lines.translation: 独处可以帮助我们在兴奋之后安静下来，在愤怒发作之后平静下来，或者仅仅让我们感到内心平和。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 16. What is one of the criticisms directed at the early research on solitude?
lines.translation: 第 16 题：针对早期独处研究的批评之一是什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 17. What do we learn about the results of the new research?
lines.translation: 第 17 题：关于新研究的结果我们了解到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 18. What did the second experiment in the new research find about solitude?
lines.translation: 第 18 题：新研究中的第二项实验关于独处发现了什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Recording 2.
lines.translation: 记录2。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In 1984, the World Chess Championship was called off abruptly, due to the withered frame of a player who was competing for the title.
lines.translation: 1984年，世界国际象棋锦标赛因一名争夺冠军的棋手身体日渐消瘦而被突然叫停。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: He wasn't alone in experiencing the extreme physical effects of the game.
lines.translation: 他并不是唯一一个在这项运动中经历极端身体影响的人。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Elite players can reportedly burn up to an absurd 6,000 calories in one day.
lines.translation: 据报道，顶尖棋手一天最多可以燃烧多达荒谬的6000卡路里。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Does that mean that thinking harder is a simple route to losing weight?
lines.translation: 这是否意味着，更加努力地思考就是一条简单的减肥途径？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Well, when the body is at rest, we know that the brain uses up a startling 20% to 25% of the body's overall energy.
lines.translation: 那么，当身体处于静息状态时，我们知道大脑会消耗全身总能量的惊人20%至25%。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This level of utilization actually makes the brain the most energy-expensive organ in the body, and yet it makes up only 2% of the body's weight overall.
lines.translation: 这种程度的能量利用实际上使大脑成为人体中能量消耗最高的器官，然而它的重量却只占人体总重量的2%。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So the more we put this organ to work, the more calories we'll burn?
lines.translation: 所以，我们越让这个器官运转，就会燃烧越多卡路里吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Technically, the answer is yes, for cognitively difficult tasks.
lines.translation: 严格来说，对于认知难度较高的任务，答案是肯定的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What counts as a "difficult" mental task varies between individuals.
lines.translation: 对不同的人而言，什么算是“困难”的脑力任务各不相同。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But generally, it could be described as something that the brain cannot solve easily using previously learned routines, or tasks that change the conditions continuously.
lines.translation: 但通常可以将其描述为：大脑无法利用此前学会的惯常方法轻易解决的事情，或者条件持续发生变化的任务。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: However, deep thinking will not burn off the calories gained from eating a sugary snack.
lines.translation: 然而，深度思考并不能消耗掉吃甜食所摄入的卡路里。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Because in relation to the brain's huge overall energy usage, which is devoted to a multitude of tasks, the energy required just to think harder is actually comparatively tiny.
lines.translation: 因为相对于大脑用于完成大量任务的巨大总体能量消耗而言，仅仅为了更加努力地思考所需的能量实际上微乎其微。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: We're unconscious of most of what uses up the brain's energy.
lines.translation: 我们没有意识到大脑的大部分能量究竟消耗在了什么地方。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: A lot of that activity is unrelated to conscious activities like learning how to sing or play the guitar.
lines.translation: 其中许多活动都与学习唱歌或弹吉他这类有意识的活动无关。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The brain is able to allocate blood (and thus energy) to particular regions that are being active at that point.
lines.translation: 大脑能够将血液（因而也包括能量）分配到当时正在活动的特定区域。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But the overall energy availability in the brain is thought to be constant.
lines.translation: 不过，人们认为大脑整体可利用的能量是恒定的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So, while there might be significant increases in energy use at localized regions of the brain when we perform difficult cognitive tasks, when it comes to the whole brain's energy budget overall, these activities don't significantly alter it.
lines.translation: 因此，当我们执行困难的认知任务时，大脑局部区域的能量使用量可能会显著增加，但就整个大脑的总体能量预算而言，这些活动并不会对其产生显著影响。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So, why did the chess champion grow too skinny to compete in his chess competition?
lines.translation: 那么，为什么那位国际象棋冠军会瘦到无法参加他的国际象棋比赛呢？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The general consensus is that it mostly comes down to stress and reduced food consumption, not mental exhaustion.
lines.translation: 普遍的共识是，这主要归因于压力和食物摄入量减少，而不是精神疲劳。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Keeping your body pumped up for action for long periods of time is very energy demanding.
lines.translation: 长时间让身体保持随时行动的状态会消耗大量能量。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: If you can't eat as often or as much as you can or would normally—then you might lose weight.
lines.translation: 如果你无法像平时那样频繁进食，或者无法吃下平时那么多食物，那么你可能会体重下降。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 19. What do we learn about the brain when the body is at rest?
lines.translation: 第 19 题：当身体处于休息状态时，我们对大脑有何了解?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 20. What does the speaker say about the consumption of the brain's energy?
lines.translation: 第 20 题：说话者关于大脑能量消耗说了什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 21. What do we learn about the overall energy availability in the brain?
lines.translation: 第 21 题：关于大脑的整体能量可用性，我们了解到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Recording 3.
lines.translation: 记录3。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Tell me about yourself.
lines.translation: 跟我说说你自己吧

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This common question is actually a critical test of a job candidate's communication skills, so it's important not to give an unprepared response or mess it up.
lines.translation: 这个常见问题实际上是对求职者沟通能力的一项重要考验，因此不要毫无准备地作答或把事情搞砸，这一点很重要。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: "Tell me about yourself" is often the first question professional career coaches prepare people for when they give interview guidance.
lines.translation: “介绍一下你自己”通常是专业职业教练在提供面试指导时，首先帮助人们准备的问题。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's the opportunity for the candidate to take control of the narrative and tell their story in a way that really matters to their audience.
lines.translation: 这是求职者掌控叙述、以一种真正对听众有意义的方式讲述自己经历的机会。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It takes hard work and extensive preparation to answer this question well.
lines.translation: 要很好地回答这个问题，需要付出艰苦努力并进行充分准备。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: When a person goes to a job interview, their interviewer has presumably read their résumé, so they don't need to repeat the information.
lines.translation: 一个人去参加求职面试时，面试官大概已经读过他的简历，因此他不需要重复其中的信息。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But that's what most people will do, as it's their instinct to recite things that are already on their résumé.
lines.translation: 但大多数人都会这样做，因为他们本能地会复述简历上已经写有的内容。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's important for job seekers to do their homework on two crucial aspects.
lines.translation: 求职者有必要在两个关键方面做好准备。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: First, they are not just telling someone a fact about themselves.
lines.translation: 首先，他们并不只是在告诉别人一个关于自己的事实，而是在讲述一个故事，而故事需要花费心力来构思。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They're telling a story, and stories take work to create.
lines.translation: 想出一个好故事，意味着要反思：是什么让他们的职业成就成为令自己感到自豪的事情，以及这些成就凸显了哪些优势。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Coming up with a good story means getting reflective about what made their career accomplishments something they're proud of and what strengths those accomplishments highlight.
lines.translation: 求职者不应挑选一个宽泛的、笼统的优势来展开，例如“我很聪明，我工作努力，而且我能把事情办成”。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Candidates shouldn't pick a broad general strength to elaborate on, such as "I'm smart, I work hard and I get things done." To come up with multiple career accomplishments or examples for different interview questions, job seekers should talk with others, especially people who know them, partners, friends or co-workers who will bring up different stories than the ones they remember.
lines.translation: 为了针对不同的面试问题想出多个职业成就或事例，求职者应该与他人交谈，尤其是那些了解自己的人、伴侣、朋友或同事，因为他们会提起一些与求职者记得的不同的故事。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Secondly, candidates should know what's at stake for the company with this job opening.
lines.translation: 其次,候选人应该知道 公司在职位空缺时 所牵涉的利害关系

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What they really are asking you is "Tell me why you are going to help me." If the person is a prepared candidate, they should have already figured out those things.
lines.translation: 他们真正问你的是"告诉我为什么你要帮我" 如果这个人是准备好的候选者 他们应该已经知道这些事了

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They've read the job description and researched the company on the Internet.
lines.translation: 他们阅读了工作说明 并在互联网上对公司进行了研究

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What job applicants ought to be looking for is what the company is up to, what they are trying to accomplish and what is preventing them from accomplishing those things.
lines.translation: 求职者应该寻找的是公司正在从事的工作、他们正在试图完成的工作以及阻碍他们完成这些工作的因素。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: How long should it take to answer?
lines.translation: 回答需要多长时间？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Around a minute.
lines.translation: 大约一分钟。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That's about right for most people's attention spans.
lines.translation: 对于大多数人的注意力持续时间来说，这个时长比较合适。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Under a minute could seem rushed, while over two minutes will start to feel more like a speech.
lines.translation: 不到一分钟可能会显得过于仓促，而超过两分钟就会开始更像是在演讲。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But the length of the answer is not an exact science, and candidates need to keep their career story focused and tailored to their audience.
lines.translation: 但答案的长度并没有绝对标准，求职者需要让自己的职业经历叙述保持重点突出，并根据听众进行调整。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 22. What does the speaker say about the job interview question "tell me about yourself"?
lines.translation: 第 22 题：说话者对于求职面试问题"介绍一下你自己"是怎么说的?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 23. What will most people do when they come to a job interview?
lines.translation: 第 23 题：大多数人在参加求职面试时会做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 24. Why should job seekers talk with partners, friends and co-workers?
lines.translation: 第 24 题：为什么求职者应该与伴侣、朋友和同事交谈?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 25. What other important preparations should job seekers make before an interview?
lines.translation: 第 25 题：求职者在面试前还应做哪些重要准备?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That's the end of listening comprehension.
lines.translation: 听觉理解到此结束
